spots.cost: PR1 fully reopened Apr 2026 after the wildfire closure. Full-trail ticket EUR10.50/person 13+ (kids 12 and under free but must be registered); the Arieiro-Pedra Rija segment stayed two-way with a EUR4.50 partial ticket during phased reopening — confirm which ticket the out-and-back needs on SIMplifica when booking. Arieiro parking reportedly EUR4.50. The summit viewpoint itself needs no trail ticket.
spots.climate: At 6,000 ft: June highs only 50-59 F and windy — pack fleece and windbreakers. Mornings are usually clear and cloud builds by mid-morning: this is the cloud lottery, and it is exactly why the plan holds five Madeira nights. Check the Arieiro webcam the same morning before committing.
spots.saveHtml: Save The family version is the out-and-back from Arieiro to the Ninho da Manta and Pedra Rija balconies (~1.2-2 km each way) — the postcard "Stairway to Heaven" staircase views without the full traverse, which is too strenuous for the 8-year-old.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge If you skip the rental car, a sunrise shuttle runs about EUR35-40/person (EUR140-160 family) door-to-door — otherwise drive up 60+ minutes before sunrise, because the summit lot fills and police close the road when it overflows.

spots.cost: Porto Moniz developed pools: EUR3/person (lifeguards, changing rooms; the rugged free Cachalote pools sit next door). Parking ~EUR1.50-3/hr. Fanal is free — the ancient laurel trees are steps from the free marked lot on ER110.
spots.climate: June: Porto Moniz sits on the cooler north coast — pool water is Atlantic-brisk (~66-68 F) inside sun-warmed lava rims. Fanal at ~3,800 ft runs a genuine fog lottery: afternoons when cloud sits on the plateau give the spooky look; clear days give cow pastures instead.
spots.saveHtml: Save Swim the developed pools for about EUR12 total — the cheapest "whoa" swim of the entire trip, volcanic rock rims and crashing surf included.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Lunch at Sea View's rooftop over the pools (~EUR60-80 family) so the kids can watch waves detonate on the lava while eating burgers.

spots.climate: June: the peninsula is the dry, desert-colored end of Madeira — zero shade, strong wind, full sun. Start 8-9 AM, bring hats and 2+ liters of water. There's a café at Cais do Sardinha midway.
spots.saveHtml: Save Turn around at the Ponta do Furado viewpoint if the 8-year-old fades — the striated-cliff money views come in the first half of the trail.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Post-hike pizza in Machico (Alforno) or a Caniçal grill lunch turns the hot morning into an easy half-day before the Monte toboggan afternoon.

The stuff nobody tells you

Operational rules that keep this from turning into a pretty but fragile itinerary.

  • Book in roughly this order

    1. Multi-city protected airfare; this is the go/no-go gate.
    2. Refundable apartments in Funchal, Palma, and Playa de Muro/Alcudia.
    3. Automatic rental cars on both islands.
    4. SIMplifica Madeira trail slots when the 2027 dates open.
    5. Drach / Soller / boat decisions only after flights and lodging are within the preferred maximum.

  • Rules that protect the trip

    • Lisbon buffer is not optional. FNC wind is the one operational hazard Madeira brings.
    • Do not chase every Mallorca cala. The north beach base is there to reduce driving.
    • Return Monday Jun 21. No extension can touch Jun 24-26.
    • Use shade aggressively. Mallorca beach days fail when the kids overheat before lunch.

items: Passports: Schengen requires validity 3+ months after planned EU departure and issue within the last 10 years (EU); renew before winter if anyone is close.
ETIAS: no July 2026 action; the U.S. State Dept. says ETIAS is planned for late 2026, so apply only after the official system launches (State Dept.).
Insurance: compare family medical/trip coverage after the first meaningful deposit; waiver timing is policy-specific, so do not wait until final payment if coverage matters.
Re-check Madeira trail closures and Mallorca heat/wind before hike/boat days.

preDepartureTodos.callout: Why this no longer says "act now" for flights: airline seats may become searchable about 11 months out, but that is not the cheapest cash-buy signal. Expedia 2026 Air Hacks found 180+ day bookings were the most expensive category in its data; Going puts international trips in a 2-8 month window, and Google Flights says U.S.-Europe trips cluster around 94 days out with risk rising inside 50 days. Track now, buy early only for award seats, unusually good protected routing, or a fare already inside budget.
